component_notes: Pictograph of a tree — trunk, branches up, roots down
ancient_form_notes: Oracle bone shows a tree with roots and branches symmetrically

component_notes: woman 女 + child 子. Historically: mother and child = good
ancient_form_notes: Bronze script shows a woman holding a child

component_notes: Pictograph of a person walking — two legs in profile
ancient_form_notes: Oracle bone is clearly a walking figure in side profile

component_notes: Pictograph of a crescent moon — the two lines inside represent its glow
ancient_form_notes: Oracle bone shows a simple crescent. Compare to 日 (sun) which is full circle
tang_usage: 月 appears constantly in Tang poetry — Li Bai's most famous poem begins 床前明月光

component_notes: Pictograph of three mountain peaks — centre peak tallest
ancient_form_notes: Oracle bone is almost identical to the modern character. Very direct pictograph.
modern_phrases: 上山 (shàngshān) — go up the mountain

component_notes: Pictograph of flowing water — a central current with smaller streams or droplets on each side
ancient_form_notes: Oracle-bone forms show a winding stream with marks for eddies or droplets

component_notes: Pictograph of flames rising from a central fire
ancient_form_notes: Oracle-bone forms show a central flame with smaller tongues of fire on each side

component_notes: Pictograph of an open mouth — the square outline marks its boundary
ancient_form_notes: Early forms are a simple rounded or rectangular outline of a mouth

component_notes: Pictograph of the heart, extended to feelings, thought, and intention
ancient_form_notes: Early forms curve around a central mark, suggesting the physical heart and its chambers

component_notes: Pictograph of a hand with fingers above the palm and wrist; its side form is 扌
ancient_form_notes: Early forms show the outline of a palm, several fingers, and a wrist

component_notes: Pictograph of scattered grains of rice around a central stalk or line
ancient_form_notes: Early forms show small grain marks arranged around a central stem

component_notes: food radical 饣 + phonetic 反; the food side points toward meals and eating
ancient_form_notes: Traditional 飯 preserves the full food component 食 on the left, later simplified to 饣
modern_phrases: 吃饭 (chī fàn) — eat / have a meal

component_notes: Pictograph of a cut of meat; as a component it often appears in body-related characters
ancient_form_notes: Early forms show the outline and inner markings of a piece of flesh

component_notes: Pictograph of a fish with head, body, and tail; simplified from 魚
ancient_form_notes: Oracle-bone forms are strongly pictorial, showing a fish body, tail, and fins

component_notes: grass/plant radical 艹 + 采, suggesting plants gathered or picked for food
ancient_form_notes: The top plant component links the character to vegetation; 采 contributes the idea of gathering and the sound
